paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: show the Ollama Cloud credit balance and recent usage as a Settings section
, with an in-page API key editor.
# dsh-ollama-quota

DeepSeek Harness plugin that owns the **provider quota dock** at the sidebar foot: Ollama
Cloud cred

it, ChatGPT **Codex subscription quota**, and the **DeepSeek API balance** with its
peak/off-peak pr

ice phase. One package, one off-peak engine, one `sidebar.footer.action` cell
that shows every provi

der on one line and opens into their full cards, plus the Ollama Settings
section that carries the f
ull rule, the usage report, and the API key editor.

The package name and the Ollama card predate the merge; the cards themselves are independent,
so one
provider can be read without the others (see Configuration).

Ollama moved the account to a credit model: `GET https://ollama.com/api/usage` no longer
carries the

old `limits.session` / `limits.weekly` windows (it answers a
`range`/`totals`/`buckets` report inst

ead), so readers built on that shape fail with
**"Could not parse the response · no limits object"**

. The remaining credit now comes from
`GET https://ollama.com/api/balance`, which is what this plugi

maining credit now comes from
`GET https://ollama.com/api/balance`, which is what this plugin reads.
## Data sources
| Provider | Endpoint | Role |
| Ollama Cloud | `GET https://ollama.com/api/balance` | primary: `included.balance_usd`, `included.a

llowance_usd`, `included.period`, `purchased.balance_usd` |
| Ollama Cloud | `GET https://ollama.com

/api/usage?range=24h\|7d\|30d` | advisory: `totals` (cost, requests, tokens) and daily `buckets` |
|
DeepSeek | `GET https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance` | `is_available` plus one `balance_infos` en

try per currency, split into `granted_balance` and `topped_up_balance` |
| Codex | `POST /api/codex-
subscription/usage` | the subscription plugin's own quota channel, called from the page over the Con
ion/usage` | the subscription plugin's own quota channel, called from the page over the Connection |

Ollama endpoints take `Authorization: Bearer <Ollama Cloud key>`; DeepSeek takes the same with
`DEEP

SEEK_API_KEY`. A failure on the Ollama usage report never hides a healthy balance; it
renders as an

inline note inside the usage card. The usage report is re-read on its own slower
interval (`usageRef
reshMs`) because its wide window barely moves.

The Codex card never touches the ChatGPT OAuth grant: it reuses the channel
`dsh-codex-subscription`

publishes for its own UI, so the quota it shows is the same number that
plugin would show, and the

grant and its refresh stay owned by that plugin. Its only coupling is
that channel's name and payloa
d shape (verified against `dsh-codex-subscription` 2.5.9).
## What it shows
| Row | Source |

| Remaining included credit | `included.balance_usd` of `included.allowance_usd` |
| Used share bar

| `allowance - balance` over `allowance` |
| Purchased credit | `purchased.balance_usd` |
| Allowanc

e period | `included.period.from` → `included.period.until` |
| Spend, requests, input/cached/output

tokens | `usage.totals` over `usageRange` |
| Daily spend strip | `usage.buckets[].usage_usd` (max

31 buckets) |
| Off-peak state and countdown | computed from the browser clock: peak pricing runs we

ekdays 12:00–18:00 UTC, everything else is off-peak |
| Key source | which credential reference reso

lved |
| API key editor | `remote.credentials.describe(refs)` / `set(ref, value)` / `unset(ref)` ove
r the DSH Remote (`remote.credentials` is a declared inject edge) |
Per-model request counts are not shown: the endpoint stopped reporting them.
### Sidebar widget

The plugin registers **one** `sidebar.footer.action` cell: a single line that stays visible at all
t

imes, not only while Settings is open. Collapsed, it lines up every provider on one row — a
brand-co

loured mark, an optional rate-phase dot, and one number each — so the state is readable
without open
ing anything. There is no phase text: **green dot = off-peak, red dot = peak**.
| Tile | Shows while collapsed | Title (hover) |
| Ollama | remaining included credit, plus the phase dot | remaining, phase, countdown to the next b

oundary |
| Codex | the highest used share of the subscription windows | the provider name |
| DeepS
eek | total balance, plus its own phase dot | the provider name and its phase |

Pressing the row expands it in place into the full per-provider cards: the Ollama card (remaining
cr

edit, the 30-day spend, phase countdown, the 24h strip on the **browser's local clock**), the
Codex

card (each window's meter, reset credits, reset countdown) and the DeepSeek card (top-up vs
granted
credit, its own peak/off-peak phase and strip). Pressing it again collapses the row.
The marks are drawn inline (a letter in the provider's colour) so the bundle stays a single classic
script with no image assets.
The collapsed 56px rail keeps the credit and a compact `H:MM` countdown.

Ollama applies off-peak pricing outside 12:00–18:00 UTC on weekdays and all day at weekends, so
the
peak window is the only interval whose end is a peak start.

The Settings section carries the same state as an additional card with the full rule text, the
local
peak window, the current local time, and both countdowns.

## Configuration
The row reads these fields, all optional (`cordis.patch.yml`):
| Field | Default | Meaning |
| `keyEnvs` | `[OLLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY, OLLAMA_API_KEY]` | credential references tried in order; the f

irst is what the editor writes |
| `apiBase` | `https://ollama.com` | API origin |
| `usageRange` |

`30d` | usage window, one of `24h`, `7d`, `30d` |
| `refreshMs` | `60000` | balance refresh interval

, minimum `5000` |
| `usageRefreshMs` | `300000` | usage-report interval, minimum `60000`; `?force=1

` or a new key re-reads it |
| `timeoutMs` | `15000` | per-request timeout |
| `deepseek.keyEnvs` |

`[DEEPSEEK_API_KEY]` | DeepSeek credential references tried in order |
| `deepseek.apiBase` | `https

://api.deepseek.com` | DeepSeek API origin |
| `deepseek.refreshMs` | `60000` | how long one DeepSee

k balance read is reused (15000–3600000) |
| `deepseek.timeoutMs` | `15000` | DeepSeek per-request t

reused (15000–3600000) |
| `deepseek.timeoutMs` | `15000` | DeepSeek per-request timeout |
